scoring_justification: The checker recomputes the fcc/liquid phase boundaries from the agent's raw CSV using the known Redlich-Kister coefficients and lattice stabilities via pycalphad; it does not trust a self-reported metric. This is a T1 recompute from the raw artifact.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference phase boundary coordinates for the Fe-Cu-Ni system at 1373–1673 K
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Recomputed by the checker at runtime from the paper's own Redlich-Kister coefficients (Table 1) and lattice stabilities (Table 2) using pycalphad, guaranteeing consistency with the paper's model.
hidden_assets.generation_method: The checker defines a pycalphad Database with the exact coefficients, runs equilibrium calculations on a fine composition grid, and extracts tie-line endpoints as reference points.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The reference is the direct computational output of the paper's published thermodynamic parameters; no arbitrary or external data is used.

outputs.description: Computed fcc/liquid phase boundary coordinates for the Fe-Cu-Ni system at temperatures from 1373 K to 1673 K. Each row gives the mole fractions of Cu, Fe, Ni and the phase (fcc or liq) for a point along the boundary.

output_contract.notes: The solver may produce multiple tie-line endpoints; all are valid as long as they satisfy the equilibrium conditions. The checker compares against hidden reference coordinates using a spatial tolerance in composition space.

steps.description: Validate phase boundary coordinates against recomputed reference boundaries using spatial tolerance.
